📌 Token Vesting: Why Team and Investor Tokens Unlock Over Time

Main Points
⏺ Token vesting schedules control when founders, teams, and investors can claim their tokens
⏺ Unlocks are usually spread over months or years with cliffs and linear releases
⏺ This post explains how vesting protects projects from instant dump pressure

1️⃣ What Is Vesting — tokens reserved for insiders are locked and only become claimable at set dates
2️⃣ Cliff Period — an initial lockup (for example, 6–12 months) where no tokens unlock at all
3️⃣ Linear Unlock — after the cliff, tokens are released gradually, such as monthly over several years
4️⃣ Market Impact — large unlocks can increase sell pressure, so traders often track vesting calendars
5️⃣ Trust Signal — transparent vesting shows that core contributors are aligned for the long term, not just a quick exit

Final Thoughts

Token vesting turns insider allocations into a time-based commitment — the longer they’re locked in, the more skin in the game the project really has.

The Pentagon’s Minab investigation found that two U.S. Tomahawks hit Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School after a chain of preventable failures: stale intelligence, compressed target approval, missing civilian-harm review and excessive faith in AI-assisted targeting.

The strike on February 28 killed at least 123 children and more than 150 people overall, according to officials familiar with the inquiry. The Pentagon still has not publicly accepted responsibility. 

President Trump has suggested Tehran was to blame and in July he said nobody might ever be able to establish what happened. Pentagon personnel reportedly knew within hours that the U.S. was responsible.

The site had once belonged to an IRGC naval unit. By 2017, satellite imagery showed new walls and entrances separating it from the military compound. 

By 2018, the location showed painted school walls, a soccer field, line-up zones and playground markings. The school operated openly, had a website and appeared on Google Maps. 

One analyst had flagged changes as early as 2019, but the note sat in a system disconnected from the principal military intelligence database. The target library kept calling a school an IRGC facility.

Maven Smart System, Palantir’s AI-enabled military platform, helped turn that obsolete classification into a recommended first-day target. 

CENTCOM personnel expected the system to flag stale intelligence or contradictions. Palantir says Maven does not own the underlying data and bears no responsibility for gaps in it. 

After Minab, the company added a feature to re-review intelligence, detect target-disqualifying factors and flag information human reviewers had missed. The product update arrived after 123 children did not.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had cut Pentagon civilian-harm-mitigation staff by roughly 90%, leaving fewer than 20 people across the relevant teams. 

CENTCOM’s unit fell from 10 people to one. No civilian-harm specialist reviewed Minab before the strike. 

Meanwhile, the administration demanded more than 1,000 Iranian targets hit in the war’s first 24 hours. The kill chain was asked to process years of neglected target files in days.

On March 2, Hegseth called the campaign “the most lethal and precise air power campaign in history,” free of “politically correct wars.” 

The precision system then fired two Tomahawks at an elementary school it had been told was a military base.

The UN Fact-Finding Mission on Iran concluded there were reasonable grounds to believe the Minab strike and another U.S. strike that day amounted to war crimes. 

It said Washington had failed to take all feasible measures to verify that the school was a military target. The Pentagon says the investigation remains ongoing. The dead children have already received the final version of the report.

🌐 Coldcard hacker uses THORChain to swap stolen BTC 

📣 A hacker associated with the third wave of Coldcard wallet thefts began converting stolen Bitcoin into Ether through THORChain on Sept. 3, according to Galaxy Research’s Alex Thorn. The transactions moved approximately 10% of the Bitcoin controlled by that attacker. Roughly 90% remained at its original addresses when he published the update. 

🔖 Researchers traced the swaps through THORChain to a newly identified Ethereum address. Thorn said he shared the address with law enforcement, crypto companies and other organizations monitoring the stolen assets. However, not every transaction succeeded. Thorn said the hacker appeared to be experiencing technical problems while attempting to process the swaps.

🔔 The cause of the refunds was not immediately confirmed. Possible explanations include liquidity limitations, transaction settings or protocol safeguards, but no verified technical assessment had established the reason. The movement represented the first detected onchain transfer from the original addresses associated with the first three attack waves, according to Thorn. Analysts will now monitor whether the resulting ETH moves to centralized exchanges, bridges or privacy services.
